Luka Doncic voices support amid Lakers ownership change to Iger and Kushner
Luka Doncic addressed the Los Angeles Lakers' latest ownership transition on Aug. 12, expressing his support for new owners Bob Iger and Josh Kushner after Mark Walter sold the team for a record $12.5 billion valuation. This marks another significant change for Doncic, who joined the Lakers following a trade from the Dallas Mavericks and quickly formed a strong relationship with Walter.
Walter's sale comes just one year after he acquired majority control of the franchise from Jeanie Buss and her family, paying $2.5 billion less than its current valuation. With Iger and Kushner now taking over, Doncic shared his thoughts on social media: "Being a Laker means everything to me, and I’m excited to get back on the court and bring a championship to LA. I’ve gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise. I look forward to…"
Following LeBron James’ departure in free agency this offseason, Doncic is set to become the primary face of the Lakers franchise as it enters another era under new leadership. The article notes that while it is unclear if Walter or the organization consulted Doncic during negotiations for this latest sale, he remains committed moving forward.
The upcoming season will be Doncic’s ninth in the NBA and his fifth under different ownership groups since entering the league. The original plan had been for him to work closely with Walter over an extended period; however, responsibilities now shift to Iger and Kushner as they aim to restore consistent championship contention in Los Angeles.
In preparation for training camp ahead of the 2026-27 season, Doncic plans to host his teammates at a minicamp in Slovenia later this month. This gathering is intended as an opportunity for team bonding and building chemistry among players before official practices begin.
